text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said that the main task of his government is to lay the groundwork for Lithuania's entry into the European Union in the organisation's first wave of enlargement.
- An agreement between Lithuania and Belarus on the readmission of illegal migrants might be signed in autumn.
- Industrial sales in May fell by 1.8 percent compared to April, the statistics department said.
- Ukio Bank reported a 714,000 litas net profit in the first five months of the year and 234,000 litas in losses in May.
- Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius reassured parliament that the currency board model will be scrapped gradually and the litas will not be devalued.
- Snoras Bank said that it will audit its financial results on a quarterly basis.
- Two breweries, Shvyturys and Kalnapilis, sold more beer in May than Utenos Beverages, the traditional leader of the country's beer market.
- Health Minister Juozas Galdikas said in an interview to the newspaper that his main task is to reform the country's fledging health care system by implementing a health insurance programme.
- Baltic Beverages Holding (BBH), which controls 40 percent of the beer market of the Baltic countries, is interested in Utena Beverages and would like to acquire a 50 percent stake in the company.

- The president of Swedish telecommunications company Telia Lars Berg, which is eying Lithuanian Telecom, said that after privatisation the number of employees could increase and the prices of services could go down.
